title: Trivial scalar condensed coefficients are acyclic for pro-prime-to-ell groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use a small coherent profinite site in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $K$ let $\mathcal A_K(C_F)$ be the category of internal $C_F$-modules with $C_F$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline K(S)=C(S,K)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and let $R\Gamma_K$ be the ordinary total right derived invariant-submodule functor [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Give the regular module $C_F$ the trivial $K$-action. If every finite continuous quotient of $K$ has order prime to $\ell$, the canonical augmentation
$$\eta_{K,F}:C_F[0]\longrightarrow R\Gamma_K(C_F[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. Here $[0]$ places a module in cochain degree zero, and the augmentation is induced by the inclusion of invariant sections into an injective resolution, with $\Gamma_K(C_F)=C_F$. This concerns ordinary internal condensed modules and the noncomplete norm-topological $\Omega$, with no completion or restriction to locally constant functions.

proof.text: Put $A=C_F$. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] with $G=K$ and $N=A$ with trivial action. This gives $R\Gamma_K(A[0])\cong\operatorname{Tot}_{n\ge0}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline K^n],A[0])$, using compatible nonnegative resolutions and the inhomogeneous group-nerve faces. The unit is the invariant inclusion in bar degree zero. This is a computation in ordinary internal modules, with derived internal Hom still present.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the scalar tame-kernel input: derived internal bar model

proof.text: For each $n$, the set $K^n$ is profinite. Apply [lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic] to $P=K^n$. It identifies the resolution column with $\mathcal C_F^n(K)[0]$, with sections $C(S\times K^n,F)$. Naturality in $P$ identifies every nerve face with precomposition; the first face is also of this form because the coefficient action is trivial. Thus the column augmentations form one map from $\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ to the first-quadrant resolution double complex in step 1. They satisfy the chain and zero-next-resolution-differential equations since they come from the resolution augmentation. Each is a quasi-isomorphism by the cited analytic lemma. The total augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation]. Consequently $\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ represents the derived bar total, with its degree-zero augmentation unchanged.

proof.text: Use the complexes $\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)$ and $\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ of [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-cochain-finite-quotient-descent]. The finite-quotient hypothesis in that lemma is exactly the hypothesis on $K$ here. Its specified inclusion $\iota$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and in degree zero both complexes equal $A$ and $\iota^0=1_A$. This is the analytic comparison needed for noncomplete $F=\Omega$; no finite-subextension-valued or completed replacement of a continuous cochain is made.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the scalar tame-kernel input: compare finite-quotient and all-continuous cochains

proof.text:
Compute the finite-quotient complex directly. Locally on a profinite test set $S$, a section $c$ of $\mathcal L_F^n(K)$ is represented by a function on $S\times Q^n$, where $Q=K/U$ is finite and $U$ is open normal. If $dc=0$ after sheafification, refine the cover so this equation holds for its representative; passing to a smaller open normal subgroup accommodates any further finite quotient. Write $m=|Q|$. For $n\ge1$ set
$$b(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1})=\frac{(-1)^n}{m}\sum_{h\in Q}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1},h).$$
This is continuous in $S$ and factors through the same finite quotient in the remaining group variables. Sum $(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n,h)=0$ over $h$. In its penultimate term replace $g_nh$ by $h$, which permutes $Q$. The other terms are precisely the differential of the displayed sum, and the last term is $(-1)^{n+1}m c$. Hence $db=c$. For $n=1$ the same equality says that the finite-group homomorphism $c$ is zero. All operations are finite sums and multiplication by the constant $m^{-1}\in F$, valid for both fields. The order assumption makes $m$ an $\ell$-adic unit; no infinite averaging is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the scalar tame-kernel input: explicit finite averaging and its differential identity

proof.text: The preceding local primitives mean that the image and kernel sheaves agree in every positive degree of $\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)$. There are no negative terms. In degree zero the differential is zero because the action is trivial, and $\mathcal L_F^0(K)=A$ since $K^0=\{1\}$. Therefore the map $A[0]\to\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)$ which is the identity in degree zero is a quasi-isomorphism. Localization at quasi-isomorphisms as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] makes it an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the scalar tame-kernel input: cohomology of the augmented finite-quotient complex

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism of step 5, $\iota$ of step 3, the total augmentation of step 2, and the inverse bar-model isomorphism of step 1. Its first two maps are identities in degree zero, its column maps are the canonical resolution comparisons, and [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] identifies the final augmentation with inclusion of invariant sections. The resulting map is thus the specified $\eta_{K,F}$, which is an isomorphism. For $K=1$ all these augmentations reduce to the identity. The same proof applies separately to $F=E$ and $F=\Omega$.

Step 1: lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar with A=C_F and trivial N=A gives the derived bar total and the invariant-inclusion normalization. Step 2: node 1 (degree-zero concentration of RHom(A_F[P],A_F) and its naturality), applied at P=K^n, plus lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation. I checked the tool's hypotheses: the first index is the resolution degree, a composed with d_{0,1} is zero because A->J^0->J^1 is zero, and the first face commutes because A->J^0 is equivariant and A is trivial. The tool use is declared in split_report and accepted as a generic black box. Step 3: node 2's iota; in degree zero L^0=C^0=A. Step 4: I recomputed the averaging. Summing dc over h gives da=(-1)^n m c, so b=(-1)^n a/m; for n=1, c=0. This needs only m invertible, which holds in characteristic 0, so all the prime-to-ell content sits in node 2. Steps 5-6: the quasi-isomorphism A[0]->L and the composite equal eta, with K=1 the identity. New nodes: B1-B3 OK, blueprint via is the item plus the inherited chain, and searches are recorded. They are not duplicates: lem-sfb-profinite-constant-derived-functions, the root-tower nodes and lem-sfb-polynomial-derived-bar-comparison all keep RHom derived, and the curve-estimates cochain nodes are for discrete coefficients only.
